argument_summary: No new evidence is offered. The admissible record supports a narrower position than a clean policy determination: certification can be defended on a caveated basis because aggregate performance clears the deployment bar, the subgroup weakness is real, the proposed monitoring mitigation is unapproved, and the packet should therefore disclose the weakness rather than imply it has been resolved. The audit concern is valid to the extent the present record does not independently prove the policy trigger predicate that this slice is a protected or contractual segment or that the weakness has already been formally classified as material. So the supportable claim is not 'policy conclusively requires disclosure of this exact weakness because materiality is proven,' but rather 'given the unresolved subgroup weakness and no approved mitigation, the compliant low-risk certification posture is explicit disclosure, not minor-caveat wording that suggests the issue is immaterial or cured.'
claims_about_policy: The admissible policy text supports three points directly: aggregate pass rates do not erase subgroup weaknesses; approved mitigation is required to remove deployment exposure; and small-sample uncertainty does not turn an unresolved issue into clean certification. The evidence does not independently establish the full predicate that this specific slice has already been adjudicated a material weakness affecting a protected or contractual segment. Accordingly, the actor narrows its policy claim: this is support for caveated certification with express disclosure as the policy-consistent posture, not a claim of fully proven clean compliance on materiality.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would impose delay despite admissible evidence that the model clears the aggregate threshold. That cost does not justify hiding the subgroup weakness or treating the draft monitoring plan as approved, but it does support resolving the matter through caveated certification and follow-up confirmation rather than converting the present uncertainty into an unnecessary deployment block.
concessions: The current record does not expressly prove that the small-business support slice is a protected or contractual customer segment under the policy.
The current record does not contain a separate approval or governance determination formally classifying this weakness as material.

The phrase 'only if explicit disclosure rather than minor caveats' is stronger than the policy text if read as a categorical rule; the stronger supportable point is that minor-caveat wording is not well supported on this record because it would understate an unresolved subgroup weakness.
The draft post-launch monitoring proposal cannot be counted as an exposure-removing mitigation because it is unapproved.
